base: A solid block has a density of 0.8 grams per milliliter. Liquid water has a density of 1.0 grams per milliliter. The block is released at the surface without touching the container. What will it do?
paraphrase: A block is set on the surface of water in the middle of a tank. The densities of the block and the water are 0.8 and 1.0 grams per milliliter, respectively. How will the block move?
change: A solid block has a density of 1.2 grams per milliliter. Liquid water has a density of 1.0 grams per milliliter. The block is released at the surface without touching the container. What will it do?
rationale: The lower-density block floats and the higher-density block sinks, from the sign of buoyancy minus weight for the block when submerged.

base: The north pole of a bar magnet is brought close to the north pole of a second bar magnet. What is the interaction between these poles?
paraphrase: Two bar magnets approach each other with both of their north ends facing one another. How do the facing ends interact?
change: The north pole of a bar magnet is brought close to the south pole of a second bar magnet. What is the interaction between these poles?
rationale: Like magnetic poles repel and unlike magnetic poles attract.

base: An ordinary battery, a working light bulb, and a switch form a single loop. The switch is closed. What is the state of the bulb?
paraphrase: A working bulb is connected in series with a battery and a switch. The switch completes the circuit. What is the state of the bulb?
change: An ordinary battery, a working light bulb, and a switch form a single loop. The switch is open. What is the state of the bulb?
rationale: A closed switch provides a continuous circuit and current flows. An open switch breaks the only circuit path. Assume an appropriate battery and bulb.

base: In a sealed container, liquid water becomes solid ice. Which process took place?
paraphrase: Water inside a closed vessel has changed phase from liquid to ice. What is the name of this process?
change: In a sealed container, solid ice becomes liquid water. Which process took place?
rationale: The names for liquid-to-solid and solid-to-liquid phase transitions are freezing and melting, respectively.

base: A metal block at 50 degrees Celsius is placed in contact with a metal block at 20 degrees Celsius without external heating or cooling. What happens initially to the 50 degree block's temperature?
paraphrase: Two metal blocks, one at 20 degrees Celsius and the other at 50 degrees Celsius, touch and exchange heat in isolation. How does the hotter block's temperature first change?
change: A metal block at 50 degrees Celsius is placed in contact with a metal block at 80 degrees Celsius without external heating or cooling. What happens initially to the 50 degree block's temperature?
rationale: Energy flows as heat from the hotter object to the cooler object. The block at 50 degrees is hotter than 20 and cooler than 80.

base: A spring lies horizontally. Its left end is fixed and its right end holds a cart. The spring is compressed and the cart is released. Which way does the spring push the cart?
paraphrase: A cart is fastened to the right end of a horizontal spring with an anchored left end. When a compression of the spring is released, which way does its force on the cart point?
change: A spring lies horizontally. Its left end is fixed and its right end holds a cart. The spring is stretched and the cart is released. Which way does the spring pull the cart?
rationale: The restoring force points toward the cart's equilibrium position. Compression places the cart closer to the left anchor, and extension places it farther to the right.

base: A uniform clay lump is reshaped from a ball into a flat disk without adding clay and without changing its density. What happens to the volume of clay?
paraphrase: The same amount of uniform clay is flattened into a disk. Its density is held constant. How does the clay's volume change?
change: A uniform clay lump is reshaped from a ball into a flat disk after adding clay and without changing its density. What happens to the volume of clay?
rationale: Volume equals mass divided by density. Reshaping changes neither mass nor density, and adding clay increases mass at fixed density.

base: A light beam can pivot about its center. A 2 kilogram mass hangs 1 meter left of the pivot and a 2 kilogram mass hangs 2 meters right of it. Which side initially drops?
paraphrase: Two equal masses hang on opposite sides of a massless, freely pivoting beam. The one on the right is twice as far from the pivot as the one on the left. Which end initially goes down?
change: A light beam can pivot about its center. A 2 kilogram mass hangs 1 meter left of the pivot and a 2 kilogram mass hangs 0.5 meters right of it. Which side initially drops?
rationale: With equal masses and a horizontal beam, the larger lever arm gives the larger gravitational torque. The right lever arm is longer in the base and shorter in the change.

base: Two isolated systems contain the same solution. One system has twice the liquid volume of the other. They have equal solute concentration. Which system has more dissolved solute?
paraphrase: Two liquid samples of one solution differ in size by a factor of two and have identical concentrations. Which sample contains the greater total amount of dissolved solute?
change: Two isolated systems contain the same solute. One system has twice the liquid volume of the other. Its solute concentration is one quarter that of the smaller system. Which system has more dissolved solute?
rationale: The amount of solute is concentration times volume. The larger volume has twice as much in the base and half as much in the changed case.

base: A cart traveled 24 meters on a straight track in 8 seconds. Was its average speed greater or less than 4 meters per second?
paraphrase: Over an 8 second interval, a cart covered a distance of 24 meters on a straight course. How does its average speed compare with 4 meters per second?
change: A cart traveled 40 meters on a straight track in 8 seconds. Was its average speed greater or less than 4 meters per second?
rationale: The mean speeds are 24/8 = 3 meters per second and 40/8 = 5 meters per second.

base: A flashlight shines through empty space at two detectors. Detector A is 2 meters from the flashlight and detector B is 4 meters away. Which detector receives the first light pulse earlier?
paraphrase: A pulse begins traveling in vacuum from the same lamp toward detectors A and B. Their respective distances from the lamp are 2 and 4 meters. Which detector detects the pulse sooner?
change: A flashlight shines through empty space at two detectors. Detector A is 6 meters from the flashlight and detector B is 4 meters away. Which detector receives the first light pulse earlier?
rationale: In vacuum the transit time is distance divided by the same speed of light. The 2-meter path is shorter than 4 meters, and 6 meters is longer.

base: A diver changes depth from 12 meters below the surface of a lake to 6 meters below the surface. What happens to the surrounding water pressure?
paraphrase: While staying in the lake, a diver ascends from 12 meters underwater to 6 meters underwater. How does the ambient water pressure change?
change: A diver changes depth from 12 meters below the surface of a lake to 18 meters below the surface. What happens to the surrounding water pressure?
rationale: Hydrostatic pressure increases with depth, so it decreases on ascent and increases on descent.
